issues: One material overstatement in mitigation wording (plural ‘overlays’ vs evidenced singular ‘overlay’).

IFRS S1/S2 risk-management-process expectations are only partially met because the draft relies on the risk register attributes but does not evidence an actual ‘process’ (inputs/parameters, roles, steps); this is partly mitigated by boundaries but still leaves IFRS alignment weaker on process description.

Governance linkage required by S1/S2 (how bodies/individuals take climate risks into account) is not evidenced in the risk management evidence set; the draft avoids explicit governance claims, but the section also does not clearly cross-link to governance disclosures (if any) to satisfy connectivity expectations.
available_evidence_omitted: Scenario analysis evidence: the draft names NGFS_v4 and scenario types/horizons, but does not use any of the available scenario name examples (e.g., Net Zero 2050, Current Policies) to make the scenario set more concrete.
unsupported_claims: “Mitigation actions … include: … collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays” is broader than the available evidence, which supports “collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlay” as a recorded mitigation action but does not evidence multiple overlays or a broader overlay program.

“The Bank’s … KPIs … are used as monitoring context” is plausible but not explicitly evidenced as a defined monitoring input/process in the risk register or process documentation (only the KPI values are evidenced).
material_unsupported_claims: “Mitigation actions … include: … collateral revaluation and flood mapping overlays” (plural ‘overlays’) overstates what is evidenced (singular ‘overlay’).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “provide additional context … and are used as monitoring context” — tighten to “provide contextual information” unless there is explicit evidence that KPIs are used in monitoring routines.

“updated when assessments are revised” — evidence supports that 4 risks are marked ‘changed since prior period’, but not the trigger/discipline for updates; tighten to “the register records changes to assessments for four risks versus the prior period.”

“internal operational climate risk management … reflected indirectly through … business continuity arrangements” — acceptable as a boundary narrative, but should be clearly framed as inference rather than evidenced practice.
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: No formal climate risk appetite thresholds are evidenced; the draft explicitly states it does not describe quantitative climate risk appetite limits.
No formal climate-risk-specific policy documents or formal escalation thresholds/triggers are evidenced; the draft discloses these are not available in the source data.

No detailed controls/procedures (eg underwriting, pricing, ECL/provisioning integration) are evidenced; the draft states mitigation actions are presented as risk-specific register entries rather than a complete control framework.
Value chain coverage is constrained: no distinct upstream climate risk entries and no purely operational climate risk entries are recorded; the draft discloses this limitation.
Scenario analysis outputs are described as modelled, forward-looking inputs and not realised losses; the draft makes this explicit and avoids implying portfolio-wide application.
